get.description: Return all the nodes currently available on the Panel.

get.description: Return all the servers that currently exist on the Panel.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Text matched against the servers' name, description, UUID and external ID.

post.description: Create a new server on the system.

get.description: Show a single server transformed for the application API.

Handle request to list all users on the panel. Returns a JSON-API representation
of a collection of users including any defined relations passed in
the request.

post.description:
Store a new user on the system. Returns the created user and an HTTP/201
header on successful creation.

get.description:
Handle a request to view a single user. Includes any relations that
were defined in the request.

patch.description:
Update an existing user on the system and return the response. Returns the
updated user model response on success. Supports handling of token revocation
errors when switching a user from an admin to a normal user.

Revocation errors are returned under the 'revocation_errors' key in the response
meta. If there are no errors this is an empty array.

delete.description: Handle a request to delete a user from the Panel. Returns a HTTP/204 response on successful deletion.

get.description:
Returns the configuration information for a node. This allows for automated deployments
to remote machines so long as an API key is provided to the machine to make the request
with, and the node is known.
Retrieve a specific server from the database using its external ID.
Retrieve a specific user from the database using their external ID.

Finds any nodes that are available using the given deployment criteria. This works
similarly to the server creation process, but allows you to pass the deployment object
to this endpoint and get back a list of all Nodes satisfying the requirements.

parameters.name: memory
parameters.description: Memory the server will need, in MiB. Nodes without this much left over are left out.

parameters.name: disk
parameters.description: Disk space the server will need, in MiB. Nodes without this much left over are left out.

parameters.name: cpu
parameters.description: CPU the server will need, where each 100 is one core.

parameters.name: tags[]
parameters.description: Only return nodes carrying all of these tags.

put.description:
Stores the Hub URL and this panel's Hub-issued key. The key is only sent to
that Hub over https, so the Hub can serve beta builds this panel was
explicitly enrolled in. Called by the Hub when the panel owner enrolls it.

post.description: Installs and enables a plugin.
Downloads and installs an update for a plugin. Will throw if no update is available.
Uninstalls a plugin. Optionally it will delete the plugin folder too.

get.description: Return all the webhooks currently configured on the Panel.

post.description:
Create a new webhook on the Panel. Returns the created webhook and an HTTP/201
status response on success.

get.description:
Return the webhook types currently registered by the Panel and its plugins. These
are the accepted values for the `type` field when creating or updating a webhook.

Return the events a webhook of the given scope can subscribe to. These are the
accepted values for the `events` field.
Return data for a single webhook.

patch.description: Update an existing webhook on the Panel. Only the fields sent are changed.

delete.description: Deletes a given webhook from the Panel.

post.description:
Fire the webhook immediately with sample data, the same way the "Test Now" button
in the panel does. Pass `event` and `data` to control what is sent, otherwise a
sample event matching the webhook's scope is used.

The delivery is queued, so the response only confirms it was dispatched. Read the
result from the webhook's `deliveries` include afterwards.

alias.description: Friendly hostname shown in place of the IP address in the Panel.

ports.description: Ports to create allocations for on the given IP address.

name.description: Name the mount is shown under in the Panel.

description.description: Free form text describing the mount.

name.description: Name the node is shown under in the Panel.

description.description: Free form text describing the node.

public.description: Whether the node can be picked by automatic deployment.

fqdn.description: Domain name or IP address the Panel reaches Wings on.

scheme.description: Protocol the Panel uses to reach Wings. Use `https` unless the node sits behind a proxy that terminates TLS.

behind_proxy.description: Whether Wings sits behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS for it.

memory.description: Memory the node makes available to servers, in MiB.

memory_overallocate.description: Percentage of memory that may be handed out beyond the limit. Use `-1` for unlimited and `0` to allow none.

disk.description: Disk space the node makes available to servers, in MiB.

disk_overallocate.description: Percentage of disk space that may be handed out beyond the limit. Use `-1` for unlimited and `0` to allow none.

cpu.description: CPU the node makes available to servers, where each 100 is one core.

cpu_overallocate.description: Percentage of CPU that may be handed out beyond the limit. Use `-1` for unlimited and `0` to allow none.

daemon_base.description: Absolute path on the node where server files are stored.

daemon_sftp.description: Port Wings listens on for SFTP connections.

daemon_sftp_alias.description: Hostname shown to users for SFTP connections when it differs from the node FQDN.

daemon_listen.description: Port Wings listens on for API requests from the Panel.

daemon_connect.description: Port the Panel connects to Wings on when it differs from the listen port, such as behind a proxy.

maintenance_mode.description: Whether the node is in maintenance mode, which stops its servers from being started.

upload_size.description: Largest file that may be uploaded through the file manager, in MiB.

tags.description: Tags used to steer automatic deployment towards or away from this node.

database.description: Name of the database to create. The final name is prefixed with the server ID, and must not already be in use by this server.

remote.description: Addresses the database user may connect from. Use `%` to allow any address.

host.description: ID of the database host the database is created on.

external_id.description: Identifier from your own system, stored alongside the server so you can match the two up later.

name.description: Name the server is shown under in the Panel.

description.description: Free form text describing the server.

user.description: ID of the user who owns the server.

egg.description: ID of the egg the server runs, which decides its default startup command, variables and images.

docker_image.description: Docker image the server container is built from. Defaults to the egg's first image when omitted.

startup.description: Command run inside the container to start the server. Defaults to the egg's startup command when omitted.

environment.description: Values for the egg's environment variables, keyed by variable name.

skip_scripts.description: Skip the egg's install script when deploying the server.

oom_killer.description: Let the kernel's out of memory killer stop the server when it exceeds its memory limit.

limits.description: Resource limits applied to the server's container.

memory.description: Memory the server may use, in MiB. Use `0` for unlimited.

swap.description: Swap the server may use, in MiB. Use `0` to disable swap and `-1` for unlimited.

disk.description: Disk space the server may use, in MiB. Use `0` for unlimited.

io.description: Block IO weight of the container relative to other containers on the node.

threads.description: Physical CPU threads the container is pinned to, such as `0`, `0-2` or `0,2`. Leave empty to let the node decide.

cpu.description: CPU the server may use, where each 100 is one core. Use `0` for unlimited.
